title: the MM2 letter D part 4 - the diakk and dinosaur walk
audit_comment: THE MM2 LETTER D PART 4 - the diakk and the DINOSAUR family of the Monster Manual II arc (the user Go call on the landed devil section). The pin-time walk from the print finds TWENTY entries on pp. 49-55: the diakk at the foot of p. 49 running onto p. 50, the DINOSAUR family head on p. 50 (doctrine only, no stat block), and the 19 dinosaur form stat blocks - Ankisaurus, Camptosaurus, Compsognathus, Dacentrurus, Deinonychus, Dilophosaurus, Dimetrodon, Euparkeria, Kentrosaurus, Mamenchisaurus, Massopondylus, Nothosaurus, Ornitholestes, Phororhacos, Podokesaurus, the giant pterosaur, Struthiomimus, Tanystropheus and Tennodontosaurus. TWENTY defs ride the R791 data_files extension in the MM1 registry schema, registry 583 -> 603. THE GRID: the 20-row DinoStats stat grid (armor class, hit dice, bonus, avgHp, attacks, xp, xp/hp, lair, move, magic resistance). THE SETTLED READS (capture primary, the 1eonline transcription and the archive.org djvu the cross-check voices): the nothosaurus xp/hp 18 (the transcription 12 its own annotation); the struthiomimus tail 2-8 (the transcription 1-8 its own error); the Nighthags word (the capture Nightbags the misread); the podokesaurus prints no prose - its paragraph prints under the struthiomimus block, the print quirk pinned verbatim; the ranged hit-dice cells read the low end (the camptosaurus 1-3 and the dimetrodon 3-to-5, the kuei precedent); the diakk or-forms read the broad max 8+8; the camptosaurus printed 0 attacks clamp to 1 in the loader. NO GAP FLIPS (the letter D box flips only when all the D parts land - the R791 no-flip precedent). NO XP-AUDIT PATCH (mm2_print rides the allowed-source list since R797). The live def walk (the one file-patch site block, no census marker) cross-checks all 20 defs against the DinoStats grid, the loader attack semantics, the podokesaurus print quirk and the registry census floor 583 -> 603.

banner.provenance: Round six of the MM2 arc, the fourth PART-LETTER walk (the user Go call on the landed devil section: the letter D continues with the diakk and the dinosaur walk pp. 49-55; the dracolisk, dragon, dragonnel, drelb, drider, duergar and dustdigger turns and the rest of D await the user call). The capture is the Curtiss PDF upload cross-checked against the independent transcription and the archive.org djvu OCR, the contested cells settled: the nothosaurus 18 xp/hp over the transcription 12; the struthiomimus 2-8 tail over the transcription 1-8; the Nighthags word over the capture Nightbags; the podokesaurus prose prints under the struthiomimus block (the print quirk, the empty text pinned); the ranged hit-dice cells read the low end (the kuei precedent); the diakk or-forms read the broad max. Census 724 -> 725, registry 583 -> 603, 20 defs, no gap flips.

tables.name: the dinosaur stat grid
tables.audit_comment: THE DINOSAUR GRID: the 20-row DinoStats stat grid (every armor class, hit-dice, bonus, avgHp, attack, xp, xp/hp, lair, move and magic-resistance cell of the diakk and the 19 dinosaur form stat blocks, in print order)
col_comments: The diakk and dinosaur form armor class cells (the or-form and slash-form cells read their best value)
The hit dice num cells (the ranged cells read the low end - the kuei precedent; the diakk or-form reads the broad max)
The hit dice bonus points (the compsognathus minus-1 rides here)
The book-average hit points (the floor(num x 3.5) + bonus formula)
The attack cells (the loader semantics: the camptosaurus printed 0 clamps to 1, the nothosaurus 1-and-2 sums to 3, the tennodontosaurus 1-and-1 sums to 2, the diakk 1-or-2 reads the max 2)
The base xp cells (the printed xp before the per-hit-point add)
The xp per hit point cells (the nothosaurus 18 settled read)
The percent in lair cells (the diakk 25, every dinosaur Nil reads 0)
The primary move cells in print inches (the first number of the print move line, the parseIntRange floor)
The magic resistance cells (the diakk 30; every dinosaur Standard reads 0)

  text = "The Glooms of Hades are populated by many monsters, the most common of which are the diakka. Diakka, unlike hordlings (the next most frequently encountered inhabitant of these planes), are more organized and dislike erratic behavior. The usual attack made by diakka when confronted by obviously strong opponents is to attempt to force them into a compact group. The diakka surround the opponents and use audible glamor to make it sound as if more diakka were coming. The largest diakka bound in and out of melee using jump and weakness as appropriate. If at least 4 of these creatures succeed in circling the opponents while giving out their odd hooting calls and croaks for 4 consecutive rounds, the sounds and rhythm of this circling dance evoke an hypnotic enfeeblement which has an area effect identical to the ray of enfeeblement spell. Each subject, regardless of magic resistance, must save vs. spell or become enfeebled as if by a 13th level magic-user, i.e., 40% strength loss for 13 rounds. Once opponents are thus affected, individual diakka use physical attacks and remaining spell-like powers to kill the prey, and then the whole flock feasts. Although these creatures are not too bright, diakka will not attack stupidly. Upon initial contact, the flock's strongest members will assess those encountered for intent and weakness. Weakness will get an opponent in far more peril than hostile intent. Very powerful, hostile creatures will only be attacked if some form of appeasement will not work. No diakk desires to be slain, regardless if it is eaten or not (as they often are by hordlings and other creatures found on the planes). Even other flocks are distrusted, because of the strong rule. Occasionally a diakk will be found on the Prime Material Plane. The appearance is always due to summoning. Nighthags (q.v.) frequently use diakka as guards. Diakka speak the hateful tongue common to Hades. They also speak their own language. There are two sorts of diakka, the tall (HD 6+6) and the broad (HD 8+8). The differences between the two are noted below, but they are not otherwise separate races, and any group will have an equal or nearly equal mixture of both sorts. In their lair there will always be 13-16 of these creatures. While a tall diakk can deliver a vicious stabbing attack with its long, sharp bill, and the broad diakk tears with its clawed arms, both sorts of diakka can also employ the following spell-like powers, 1 at a time, 1 per round, at will: weakness by touch in attack (1 per day), jump (2 per day), audible glamor (1 per day), and enfeeblement by group only (see above). Tall diakka resemble huge storks with bills, human-like heads and faces, and thin, human-like arms. Broad diakka resemble huge, squat pelicans with foreshortened bills on human-like heads. Instead of wings, these creatures have short, thick arms with huge, curving claws. Feather color is in sickening hues and combinations and varies wildly, including pea green and rusty-red orange, purple and orange and pink, and dirty yellow. Heads are feathered, but faces are brightly colored and featherless. Legs, bills, feet, claws, etc., are usually black, dark brown, maroon, or deep green. Tall diakka are very fast and give loon-like cries. Broad diakka are rather slow. They make gobbling croaks and caws while attacking.",
